# Lab notebook {#sec-notebook}

This chapter is the program's running lab notebook: the dated,
chronological record of hypotheses, pre-registrations, runs, refutations,
and course corrections, in the order they actually happened. Unlike the
rest of the book, it is *not* edited for timelessness — superseded readings
stay, marked as superseded, because the path matters.

The documentation chapters state what is currently believed and why; this
chapter records how we got there. If a claim in the clean chapters seems to
appear from nowhere, its full history is here. Every entry names the
checked-in archive key in `results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json` that holds
its numbers; the clean sections holding the current-best tables are
cross-referenced at the end of each entry.

(Iterations 1–6 — the falsification ladder, the Neumann extension, the
parametric study, the pruning study, and the 3D suite — predate this
notebook's split from the main chapters and are recorded in narrative form
in @sec-learned-bie, @sec-parametric, and @sec-3d-results.)

## Iteration 7 — the kernel-decoder fix and the first dictionary finding {#sec-nb-iter7}

*(2026-07-03; key `iteration_7_kernel_decoder_fix`.)*

**The gate (seed 17, 1,000 updates, early 8-case bank — preliminary,
now superseded).** First trained result for
`MeshTransformer(query_decoder="kernel")`; the moment and encoded-pair
rows are the checked-in ablation artifact's same-protocol controls; the
kernel row was a session artifact under `/tmp/kernel_decoder_bench`.

| query decoder (same protocol) | params | ID | freq-OOD | mode-3 response |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| moment (reference config) | 135,945 | 0.530 | 1.000 | 0.990 |
| encoded pair (factorial winner) | 130,736 | 0.144 | 0.898 | 0.142 |
| **kernel (the fix)** | 110,561 | **0.0416** | **0.1225** | **0.080** |

: The decoder gate: seed 17, 1,000 updates, early bank — single seed,
preliminary; superseded by @tbl-kernel-refbank. Kept here because the
1,000-update freq-OOD value (0.12) becomes load-bearing in the
dictionary-selection finding below. {#tbl-kernel-gate}

That read as 12.7$\times$ over the moment decoder, 3.5$\times$ over the
factorial's encoded-pair winner, and within about 20% of the
PDE-conforming panel BIE at the same budget (0.035, @tbl-h1e) while
staying PDE-agnostic. Off-axis splits held (geometry-OOD 0.064, stronger
deformation 0.093, mixed 0.061); the trained model kept the exact
contracts (superposition $1.1\times10^{-7}$, zero drive exactly 0,
similarity covariance $2.8\times10^{-7}$); and evaluation error *fell*
under boundary refinement — 0.322 $\to$ 0.032 from 32 to 256 panels —
where the moment decoder was flat at $\approx$0.27. The session-artifact
mode-response comparison:

```{python}
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Pure-mode relative L2 response by boundary harmonic mode. Moment
#|   decoder: checked-in reference_2026-07-01.json (3 seeds, reference
#|   protocol). Kernel decoder: session artifact
#|   /tmp/kernel_decoder_bench/mesh_transformer_kernel_reference.json
#|   (seed 17, 1,000 updates, early bank). The protocols differ, so read
#|   shapes, not third decimals: the moment decoder transmits modes 0-2 and
#|   nothing above (the proved nullspace); the kernel decoder responds
#|   essentially flat -- 0.08 at m=3, and 0.08-0.29 through m=12 in the
#|   artifact (m0-m8 shown to match the reference scan).
import json
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

reference = json.load(open(Path("..") / "results" / "reference_2026-07-01.json"))
moment = reference["pure_mode_relative_l2"]["mesh_transformer"]
kernel = json.load(
    open("/tmp/kernel_decoder_bench/mesh_transformer_kernel_reference.json")
)["evaluation"]["mode_response"]

modes = list(range(9))
mt = [moment[str(m)] for m in modes]
kd = [kernel[str(m)]["relative_l2_mean"] for m in modes]

x = np.arange(len(modes))
width = 0.38
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.8, 3.4))
ax.bar(x - width / 2, mt, width, color="#e34948",
       label="moment decoder (checked-in, 3 seeds)")
ax.bar(x + width / 2, kd, width, color="#2a78d6",
       label="kernel decoder (session artifact, seed 17)")
ax.axhline(1.0, color="#0b0b0b", lw=1.0, ls="--")
ax.text(8.42, 1.02, "no response", fontsize=8, color="#0b0b0b",
        ha="right", va="bottom")
ax.axvspan(2.5, 8.5, color="#e34948", alpha=0.06, lw=0)
ax.text(8.45, 1.14, "proved $m\\geq 3$ nullspace — removed",
        ha="right", fontsize=8.5, color="#52514e")
ax.set_xticks(x, [f"m={m}" for m in modes])
ax.set_xlabel("boundary harmonic mode (modes 1-4 occur in training)")
ax.set_ylabel("pure-mode relative $L^2$")
ax.set_ylim(0, 1.24)
ax.grid(axis="y", color="#e1e0d9", lw=0.8)
ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.0, 1.0))
for spine in ("top", "right"):
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Two caveats were recorded at the gate. The interior Laplacian residual
was $\approx$1.0 (the smooth MLP member is not harmonic) next to
freq-OOD 0.12 *without* operator fidelity — so the
residual-predicts-generalization association calibrated on the ladder's
value interpolators (freq-OOD 0.6–0.9 at residuals 8–10, @sec-ladder) is
evidently not a theorem. And the on-boundary trace diagnostic read
$\approx$1.5 — the singular member's jump discontinuity sits exactly on
the probe points; near-boundary *interior* error was 0.033, in line with
ID.

**The reference-bank confirmation, and the finding the gate could not
see.** Seeds 17/29/43 at 3,000 updates on the frozen 64-case bank
confirmed the fix (@tbl-kernel-refbank) — and the full dictionary's
freq-OOD had slid 0.12 $\to$ 0.487, statistically indistinguishable from
the free-form pair kernel. The near-zero-initialized smooth MLP members
had grown to absorb ID error: **training trades structure for
interpolation**. Ablating them (`kernel_mlp_members=0`) restored freq-OOD
0.0713 at identical ID. First honest caveat, recorded then: the singular
member *is* Laplace-family structure, so on other PDE families the smooth
members "may well earn their place" — queued as the off-family tests
below. *(Current tables: @tbl-kernel-refbank in @sec-kernel-decoder.)*

## Iteration 8 — Liouville: the drive-linearity wall breaks {#sec-nb-iter8}

*(2026-07-03; key `iteration_8_liouville_nonlinear_wall`.)*

Question: every drive-linear model ties at $\approx$0.79 ID on the
nonlinear Liouville suite (the superposition wall; parameter-free floor
1.06). The kernel decoder in `zero_preserving_nonlinear` mode reads drive
invariants, so it is not drive-linear. Does it break the wall, and do the
MLP members earn their place on a nonlinear PDE?

Result (1,500 steps, seeds 17/18/19, fixed-compute protocol identical to
the baselines): **wall broken and replicated** — linear control mean
0.769 (on the predicted wall), nonlinear arms 0.464 / 0.476; worst
nonlinear seed (0.564) beat the best linear seed (0.749). The MLP-member
question resolved to a **tie** ($\Delta = 0.012$ vs seed spread
$\sim$0.085). Methodological sting, recorded at the time: seed 17 alone
said "tie", seed 18 alone said "MLP wins by 0.13" — a single-seed
conclusion would have misled in *either* direction; three seeds were
necessary.

Two protocol notes from the replication. (a) 5,000-step constant-LR runs
oscillate late, and final evaluation diverged from same-step validation
(dictionary-only ID 1.337 vs val 0.410). Initially attributed to "no LR
decay, no best-checkpoint selection". **Correction (2026-07-04, logged
during iteration 13):** `liouville.py` already restores the
best-validation checkpoint — the gap is a 4-case-validation vs
16-case-evaluation gap on an unstable model (heavy-tailed per-case
errors); the remaining gap is the missing LR decay alone. (b) The
strong-form PDE residual stayed at 2.3–3.0 against a calibration where
any harmonic prediction scores exactly 2.0: $L^2$-fit training fits the
field, not the operator. *(Current tables: @tbl-liouville-arms in
@sec-liouville.)*

## Iteration 9 — screened Laplace through the full architecture {#sec-nb-iter9}

*(2026-07-03; key `iteration_9_screened_meshtransformer`.)*

$\tilde\kappa$ entered only as an operator-side global scalar; the
specialists know the PDE, the `MeshTransformer` is handed the number but
not its meaning. The generalist beat the harmonic-basis specialist ID by
$\sim$5$\times$ without knowing the PDE, stayed within $\sim$4$\times$
of the exact-Yukawa specialists that do, lost decisively at high
$\tilde\kappa$ (the expected price), and degraded *gracefully* at low
$\tilde\kappa$ where the Yukawa basis diverges 8.7–28 — the
graceful-degradation argument for harmonic-biased dictionaries.

Dictionary-selection replication, the strongest to that date: MLP members
left ID and both $\tilde\kappa$-OOD splits unchanged but destroyed
unseen-modes generalization 10$\times$ (0.184 vs 0.019, 3/3 seeds). The
ledger at that point: Laplace — destructive; screened — destructive;
Liouville — neutral. *(Current tables: @tbl-screened-arms,
@tbl-screened-specialists in @sec-screened.)*

## Iteration 10 — 3D: genericity holds; a reading that later fell {#sec-nb-iter10}

*(2026-07-03; key `iteration_10_laplace3d_meshtransformer`.)*

Dimensional genericity held end-to-end (bitwise-identical parameter
count, zero core changes; six seeds), and both arms beat the double-layer
oracle on the declared-unsolved shell tier (medians 0.380/0.458 vs
0.753) with honestly large seed variance (sd 0.20–0.33, one 1.17
dictionary-only seed).

**The reading that did not survive:** the MLP-member effect appeared to
*flip* in 3D — equal-or-better on star 6/6 seeds and modes 5/6 — and the
ledger was revised to a *span-dependent* rule: smooth members hurt where
the structured dictionary already spans the smooth corrections (the 2D
polynomial family) and help where it spans less (3D). The rule was stated
falsifiably, with the deciding experiment named: drop the 2D polynomial
members; if OOD collapses, the polynomial family is the span that made
the MLPs redundant; if not, the hypothesis is wrong. *(It was wrong —
iteration 11. The flip itself was later shown to be an artifact —
iteration 12. Current tables: @tbl-3d-meshtransformer in
@sec-3d-meshtransformer.)*

## Iteration 11 — the pre-registered 2D dictionary ablation {#sec-nb-iter11}

*(2026-07-04; key `iteration_11_dictionary_ablation_2d`.)*

Pre-registered predictions from the span hypothesis, written before the
runs: **(a)** dropping polynomial members (keeping singular+MLP) recovers
ID but destroys freq-OOD; **(b)** singular-only loses ID but stays
OOD-stable.

Outcome: **(a) half-right** — nopoly recovered ID (0.042) and freq-OOD
was destroyed relative to the structured arms (0.213) but *less* than
the full arm's 0.487: polynomial members **amplify** MLP harm, an
unpredicted interaction that remains unexplained (checked-in caveat).
**(b) refuted outright, favorably** — singular-only lost *nothing*: best
ID of the matrix (0.0375), best stronger-deformation (0.0774), freq-OOD
statistically identical to sing+poly (0.0748 vs 0.0713, tightest seed
spread 0.073–0.076). The span hypothesis died by its own test, and the
takeaway was revised to: conditioning carries the smoothness; the
dictionary carries the singularity. The 3D disentangler (p3b) was
launched the same day. *(Current tables: @tbl-dictionary-matrix,
@tbl-dictionary-seeds in @sec-dictionary-ablation.)*

## Iterations 12–13 — the disentangler, universality, and the closing rule {#sec-nb-iter12}

*(2026-07-04; keys `iteration_12_dictionary_ablation_3d`,
`iteration_13_singonly_universality`.)*

The 3D disentangler came back within the day and overturned iteration
10's flip: **the polynomial members were the problem in 3D too.**
Dropping them improved every 3D split $\sim$2$\times$ and collapsed the
shell tier's seed variance (sd 0.20–0.33 $\to$ 0.022–0.042; the 1.17-type
seeds disappeared); the MLPs had been partially compensating for
polynomial harm, and once the polynomials were gone the MLP advantage
evaporated.

The universality checks (p3cd): screened singular-only **best-in-class**
(ID 0.0099, low-$\tilde\kappa$ 0.0345 — the conditioning survives a
one-member dictionary); nonlinear Liouville singular-only **failed
catastrophically** (ID 0.9583/36.5348/2.30, seed 18 diverged) — in
nonlinear field mode the polynomial members are load-bearing. The
dictionary program closed on the rule that now heads
@sec-decoder-role: *the dictionary carries the singularity; conditioning
carries the smoothness; nonlinearity needs a smooth basis.* One
discriminator was left parked, not queued: whether the nonlinear failure
is representational or an optimization instability (a cosine-decay rescue
run decides). The iteration-8 checkpoint-selection correction (above) was
logged here. *(Current tables: @tbl-dictionary-3d in @sec-dictionary-3d;
@tbl-screened-singonly in @sec-singonly-universality.)*

## Iteration 14 — scalar-only, and the wide-scalar control {#sec-nb-iter14}

*(2026-07-04; key `iteration_14_scalar_only_2d` +
`wide_scalar_capacity_control`.)*

Do the vector channels earn their complexity? On 2D Laplace, no: scalar
singular-only (41,941 params, −60%) matched vector-ful within
$\sim$5–15% on every split, equivariance still at machine precision. Off
plain 2D, yes: screened ID degraded 2.9$\times$, 3D sphere 3.4$\times$,
star 1.9$\times$ — while modes-OOD was unchanged-or-better and the shell
tier identical with *tighter* variance (more evidence the shell error
was representational, which seeded iteration 16). The open confound —
42k vs 104k parameters — was stated in the entry and closed the same
day by the capacity-matched wide-scalar control (105,301 params): it did
**not** recover the gap (3.3$\times$ / 2.5$\times$). It was not width;
oriented inter-cell transport is genuine physics capacity; the vector
channels stay. *(Current tables: @tbl-scalar-2d, @tbl-scalar-off2d in
@sec-scalar-only.)*

## Iteration 16 — the single-layer member: a failed prediction, a better rule {#sec-nb-iter16}

*(2026-07-04; key `iteration_16_single_layer_member`.)*

Pre-registered prediction (from the representational diagnosis of the
shell tier): *shell improves dramatically; simply connected tiers
unchanged.* **Failed on both halves**: shell not fixed
(0.305/0.368/0.704 — median matching singular-only, one unstable seed)
and 2D star-bank freq-OOD regressed 2–4$\times$ (0.17–0.27 vs 0.075).
Mechanism, once seen: any member with a smooth far field — even an
exactly singular one — gets abused by SGD to absorb ID error, because
the conditioned coefficients are free where classical BIE would
determine them.

An intermediate hypothesis was recorded at the first-seed multi-body read
(`multi_body_head_to_head_partial`): a topology-*gated* (Betti-gated)
dictionary. It did not survive the full head-to-head — deep-cavity is
simply connected and the member helps there too. The refined rule that
replaced both: **two exact singular members are the default for hard
geometry; the honest cost is extrapolation on easy geometry.**

A failure was flagged at two seeds — both arms losing to the
19k-parameter pair kernel on deep-slot OOD — and **downgraded at the
third seed** (`deep_cavity_final_n3`): singpair deep-slot mean 0.240
matches-or-beats the control's 0.265; the loss was specifically the
singular-only arm (0.393). Two seeds flagged what three dismissed.
*(Current tables: @tbl-multibody, @tbl-deepcavity in @sec-single-layer.)*

## Iteration 18 — encoder depth: a null, then its resolution {#sec-nb-iter18}

*(2026-07-04; key `iteration_18_encoder_depth`.)*

Logged as **preliminary** at a single seed: enc0 — zero boundary
self-attention, 59,385 params — matched the full two-layer singpair on
multi-body (ID 0.073 vs 0.070), raising the sharpest parsimony question
of the program: does the model collapse to lift $\to$ conditioned
two-member singular decode? The pre-registered theory note said the
Dirichlet null should be *expected* ($\tfrac12 I$-dominated second-kind
Fredholm solve — nearly local) and named mixed/Neumann BCs as the real
test. Seed 18 confirmed the Dirichlet null (`runs_update_n2`); the mixed
test became iteration 19. *(Current statement: @sec-encoder-depth.)*

## Iteration 19 — the mixed-BC discriminator {#sec-nb-iter19}

*(2026-07-04; key `iteration_19_mixed_bc_discriminator`.)*

Pre-registered: encoder depth should matter on mixed BCs where it did not
on Dirichlet. Confirmed in direction with a parsimony twist: enc0
degrades on the mixed shell — as *unreliability*, not uniform
degradation (catastrophic seed 18: 0.112/0.182) — while enc1 matches
enc2 (0.051 vs 0.049). Attention earns its keep exactly where the
Fredholm structure is nonlocal, and one layer suffices. Physics note:
shell_mixed at 0.049 is 7$\times$ easier than the all-Dirichlet shell —
the explicit outer flux removes the winding-inference difficulty.
Caveats recorded: one mixed tier; drive depth held at 1 (the sharper
drive-depth sweep parked). *(Current tables: @tbl-mixed-bc in
@sec-mixed-bc.)*

## Iteration 20 — the scale ladder {#sec-nb-iter20}

*(2026-07-04; key `iteration_20_scale_ladder`.)*

Run last, after simplification, on purpose — against the
one-layer/two-member model. Decode cost measured at
$O(Q^{0.97}S^{0.96})$, $R^2 = 0.999$ (the designed dense cost); encoder
flat over the range (launch-dominated, not the wall). At product scope
($10^5 \times 10^6$, extrapolated): training memory breaks first,
$\approx$742 GiB — autograd retains the dense pair activations — with
two characterized fixes (checkpointing over query chunks, exact; or a
hierarchical backend, approximate); inference already fits one A100
($\approx$85 GB, $\sim$9–16 min per forward). Zero-shot resolution
transfer held across 16$\times$. Profiling found dead work in the dense
hot loop (`PairInvariantFeatures` computing for absent smooth members) —
queued as engineering hygiene. *(Current tables: @tbl-scale-fits,
@tbl-scale-transfer in @sec-scale.)*

## Iteration 21 — the fluid families, and the pseudoscalar wall {#sec-nb-iter21}

*(2026-07-04; key `iteration_21_fluid_families_pseudoscalar_wall`.)*

The program's first fluid benchmarks: `potential_flow.py` (exterior
potential flow from certified exterior conformal maps; freestream as a
global rank-1 drive *vector* — the first exercise of the vector-drive
path — plus a circulation pseudoscalar; target = single-valued
disturbance streamfunction) and a manufactured `boundary_layer`
two-scale family. Controls trace-informed; `MeshTransformer` arms get
raw $\{U, \Gamma\}$ only. 3,000 steps, three seeds, H100 fleet.

**The chronology, as it happened.** The smoke runs warned: early
validation flat near 1.0 on the MT arms while the pair-kernel control
descended. The full budget confirmed the flatline — `MeshTransformer`
**no-response on every seed and every split** (potential flow ID
0.98–1.00; boundary layer 0.91–1.04) against the trace-informed control
at 0.178 (potential flow) / 0.73 (boundary layer). First suspicion was a
dead input path — a wiring bug in the new global-vector drive — so a
gradient diagnostic went in:
$\partial(\text{output})/\partial(\text{freestream}) = 6359$. The path
was alive. The model was receiving the drive and *provably* could not
use it.

**The diagnosis is one line of group theory.** The disturbance
streamfunction is a 2D **pseudoscalar**: its uniform-flow part is the
wedge $U \wedge x = U_x y - U_y x$, which changes sign under
reflection. The type system builds scalars only from dot products of
polar vectors, and any function of dot invariants equals its mirror
image — a *true* scalar. No dot-only model can manufacture handedness
from unhanded inputs. The architecture was not failing to train; it was
**enforcing its own type contract** against a benchmark target that
violates it — the mirror-test refusal of @sec-typed-channels, measured
in the wild for the first time. The controls escape because the
pseudoscalar-ness arrives baked into their per-cell trace scalars.
(Circulation is itself a pseudoscalar; the benchmark is restricted to
orientation-preserving similarities for exactly that reason.)

**Fix plan (iteration 22, in flight):** (a) **velocity-vector output** —
a polar vector, representable as-is, and the natural gateway to Euler
multi-field targets; (b) a **trace-driven MT arm**, to separate
encode-solve difficulty from the type mismatch; (c) evaluate admitting
**2D pseudoscalar ($0o$) channels with a wedge product** — an extension
considered and set aside earlier in the program, which now has its first
concrete motivating failure. *(Current tables: @tbl-potential-flow,
@tbl-boundary-layer in @sec-fluid-suites.)*

## Iteration 22 — representable reformulations, and a second type finding {#sec-nb-iter22}

*(2026-07-04; key `iteration_22_representable_reformulations`.)*

The fix plan ran (p10: trace arms + velocity arms, 3,000 steps, three
seeds, H100s; the velocity arms are the program's first rank-1-output
runs — the core vector-output path was verified complete, no patch
needed).

**The chronology.** The 500-step smoke signal was already decisive in
one direction: the trace arms' validation dropped like a Laplace run —
the wall was gone the moment the target became representable. The full
matrix confirmed it: **singpair_trace ID 0.013 / geometry-OOD 0.012 /
wilder 0.045 / circulation-OOD 0.020**, fourteen times better than the
pair-kernel control *given identical data*, and the program's best
exterior-domain numbers to date. Diagnosis confirmed: the pseudoscalar
wall was pure target-type mismatch — encode–solve was never the
problem.

Then the odd number. The velocity arms broke the wall as predicted (ID
0.13–0.15, geometry-OOD 0.19) — but **circulation-OOD sat at
0.6446–0.6511 on every arm and every seed**: nine runs, three dictionary
compositions, a spread of half a percent. That is not optimization
noise; that is a constraint. The decomposition insight came from writing
the vortex term down: the circulation component of velocity is
$\Gamma\, x^{\perp} / (2\pi |x|^2)$, and with $\Gamma$ declared a
*true* scalar in the field schema, scalar $\times$ (rotated position)
is an **axial vector** — the same mirror-test refusal as iteration 21,
one type deeper. The residual decomposes *exactly*: representable
potential flow, learned; unrepresentable vortex flow, refused; the
pinned 0.647 is the norm of the refused part.

**Armijo trigger.** Direction 6's pre-registered criterion — build the
$0o$ extension only if the velocity reformulation measurably fails — is
**met**, precisely on the circulation component and nowhere else.
Iteration 23 launched: 2D pseudoscalar ($0o$) channels with the wedge
product as a typed operation, $\Gamma$ declared pseudoscalar in the
schema. Prediction registered before the runs: **circulation-OOD joins
ID** (the other splits should not move, since they never touched the
refused subspace).

One new stress axis, logged for the roadmap: far-field queries degrade
for every arm (0.43–0.88; control 1.69) — radius extrapolation beyond
the training annulus is open, and it is *not* a type problem.
*(Current tables: @tbl-potential-flow-resolved in @sec-fluid-suites.)*

  entry, prediction pre-registered in @sec-nb-iter22.
- The engineering-review item "Dead work in the dense hot loop" was tagged
  *(added 2026-07-04, found while profiling the scale study)*.
- 06's 3D results section opened "The 3D runs completed after the chapters

## Iteration 23 — the pseudoscalar extension lands {#sec-nb-iter23}

*(2026-07-05; key `iteration_23_pseudoscalar_extension`.)*

The program's first type-system extension, built against the iteration-22
Armijo trigger. Design: 2D pseudoscalar channels behind a new rank token
`"0o"`, with the **closed product set** — wedge $v \wedge w \to 0o$;
rotation $p \cdot v^{\perp} \to$ polar vector (exactly the
$\Gamma\,x^{\perp}$ product the velocity arms refused);
$p \cdot q \to 0e$; $s \cdot p \to 0o$ — pseudos riding the existing
scalar moment machinery. Circulation declared `"0o"` in the field
schema. Bitwise-default preserved (zero parameters and zero RNG draws at
pseudo width 0); 553 tests, including reflection equivariance of every
product and end-to-end model reflection tests. Arms: `kernel_pseudo`
(138,665 params), `singpair_pseudo` (132,641), `drive_pseudo_dim=8`.

**The chronology.** The build went in with the prediction already
registered (@sec-nb-iter22): circulation-OOD joins ID; other splits
unmoved. The 500-step smoke was the moment worth logging: the pseudo
arms' circulation validation **crossed the 0.647 floor** — the number
nine untyped runs could not move — and kept going. The 3-seed harvest
then *exceeded* the prediction: not only did circulation-OOD join ID,
the **entire velocity field improved** $\sim$5$\times$ (ID
0.141 $\to$ 0.028, geometry-OOD 0.191 $\to$ 0.041, wilder shapes
0.264 $\to$ 0.131). Two fresh seeds (20/21) plus fresh *untyped* control
arms at the same seeds were added to rule out a seed accident: the
controls stayed pinned at 0.6457–0.6481, the pseudo arms held, and the
result was adopted at **five seeds** — the new evidentiary bar for
headline claims.

**Why it exceeded the prediction** (post-hoc, flagged as such): 2D
potential-flow velocity is intrinsically *parity-mixed* — the doublet's
angular structure carries both $U \cdot \hat x$ and $U \wedge \hat x$
content — so wedge invariants pay everywhere in the field, not just in
the vortex term. The registered prediction ("other splits unmoved") was
therefore *wrong in the good direction*, and is recorded as such.

Parsimony held under the extension (singpair remains the best
dictionary); far-field stayed at $\sim$0.7 — confirmed as a non-type
open axis. Scope, stated at the time: $0o$ is 2D-only and **opt-in**
(the 3D analogue is the axial vector, out of scope); the default
reference configuration is unchanged (@sec-reference-config).
*(Current table and figure: @tbl-pseudo-extension, @sec-fluid-suites.)*

## Iteration 24 — the intrinsic gauge {#sec-nb-iter24}

*(2026-07-05; key `iteration_24_intrinsic_gauge`.)*

Started as a fork question: the caller-supplied `reference_length` had
always felt like the "hacky" corner of an otherwise
everything-by-construction architecture — the one input the model
*trusts* rather than derives. The gauge analysis made the discomfort
precise: any $L$ that is degree-1 homogeneous in the geometry preserves
similarity covariance, so the caller's number was never load-bearing —
only its *consistency* between training and evaluation was, and
consistency by convention is exactly the kind of contract this program
does not accept. Decision: derive $L$ intrinsically as the
measure-weighted RMS boundary radius about the center (the radius of
gyration) — fp64, differentiable, outlier-robust through the measure
weighting; sharper alternatives (max-radius and bounding-box-type
measures) fail smoothness or outlier-robustness. The explicit key stays
as a bitwise-preserved override (an aero chord is a *meaningful* gauge;
the point is that no gauge is ever *required* from outside).

Three experiments pre-registered, all confirmed: **gauge neutrality**
(intrinsic ID 0.0372 vs explicit 0.0375 at three seeds — identical
band); **convention drift** (corrupt $L$ by 3$\times$ at eval:
explicit-key arm degrades 4.64$\times$, intrinsic arm bitwise immune —
the input no longer exists; kept as a permanent demo test); the
**unconditional similarity contract** (2.9–3.1$\times$10$^{-7}$
including 0.2$\times$/5$\times$ scales).

And the bonus that justified the whole exercise twice over: testing at
$L \neq 1$ flushed out a **latent bitwise-query-independence bug** —
the pair-invariant einsum was taking a CUDA batched-GEMM path with
1-ulp drift for any $L \neq 1$, invisible until now because every
contract test ran on $L = 1$ data. Found, fixed, and the test data
de-biased. *(Current table: @tbl-intrinsic-gauge in
@sec-intrinsic-gauge; the architecture chapter's forward-pass step 1
was updated in the same change, per its contract.)*

## Iteration 25 — Euler–Bernoulli: the first multi-field suite {#sec-nb-iter25}

*(2026-07-05; key `iteration_25_euler_bernoulli_multifield`.)*

Design went in with the wall pre-registered: targets {velocity rank-1,
pressure rank-0}, pressure $p^* = (|U|^2 - |u|^2)/2$ exactly
drive-quadratic (exact Bernoulli labels, no solver; velocity odd and
pressure even under drive negation, verified exactly in the generator
tests). Multi-field output worked through the core unchanged. The
pre-registered second wall: a linear-mode arm is **bitwise drive-odd**
— its output flips sign exactly with the drive — so its even-parity
pressure response is structurally zero and its pressure error is
exactly 1.000. A designed sibling of the Liouville superposition wall.

**Chronology.** The structural proof checked out before training even
mattered: the linear arm's pressure error sat at 1.0000 $\pm$ 0.0007 on
every split of every seed — the wall held *bitwise*, five for five.
The 200-step smoke produced the iteration's anomaly: a catastrophic
circulation-OOD blowup (37–147) in the nonlinear arms — the
drive-amplitude extrapolation exploding early in training. It largely
resolved by 3,000 steps (best-arm circ-OOD 0.35): an early-training
transient, not a structural refusal, but drive-amplitude extrapolation
stays the worst split and is logged as an open stress axis. The
headline landed at five seeds: **the parity and nonlinearity mechanisms
compose** — nonlinear alone reaches pressure 0.210; nonlinear + $0o$
reaches velocity 0.031 / pressure 0.063 and dominates every split.

The pre-registered degree-grading hypothesis (grade the drive stream by
polynomial degree to target drive-quadratic fields directly) is
**demoted** to a moderate-priority open item on Armijo reasoning: the
composition result leaves it a one-split gain (circ-OOD), and one split
does not buy a mechanism. *(Current table: @tbl-euler-bernoulli in
@sec-euler-bernoulli.)*

## Iteration 26 — the stream factorization measured {#sec-nb-iter26}

*(2026-07-05; key `iteration_26_stream_factorization`.)*

The last unmeasured architectural factorization: the operator/drive
two-stream split. The control was built as an example-level wrapper
(drive re-declared as operator features, unit-drive propagation; zero
core changes; parameters matched within 0.03%) and documented as
**measurement-only** — it forfeits the zero-drive and superposition
contracts by design, so it prices the factorization but can never
replace it. Three hypotheses went in pre-registered: **H1** ID parity
on linear problems, **H2** two-stream wins freq-OOD (the motivating
belief: structural drive-linearity should extrapolate the spectrum),
**H3** the control measurably violates the contracts.

**Laplace (3 seeds).** H1 came back *better* than parity: two-stream
ID 0.0485 vs 0.0606 — a 3.6$\times$-seed-sd win at matched parameters.
Then the refutation worth logging in full. **H2 fell.** The freq-OOD
column read 0.179 for the *control* and 0.211 for the two-stream arm —
the free model slightly better, and more seed-stable. The belief that
the linearity contract was buying spectrum extrapolation had been
carried since the ladder days without ever being isolated; isolated, it
is false. What buys frequency extrapolation is the dictionary and its
conditioning — the same answer the dictionary ablations gave from the
other side. H3 quantified the gap between learned and structural
physics: the control learns *approximate* linearity (zero-drive 0.038,
superposition 0.042) and plateaus five decades above the roundoff-exact
contract.

**Liouville (3 seeds).** A statistical tie — single-stream
0.478 ± 0.097, two-stream 0.533 ± 0.145 — and the iteration's real
find hiding in the zero-drive column. The two-stream arm reads exactly
0 there, as designed. But on Liouville, zero Dirichlet data does *not*
have the zero solution — the interior is $u = \log 4$ — so the exactly
enforced value is exactly **wrong**, while the free control drifts to
0.55–0.70, closer to the physics. Zero-preservation had been treated as
physics; it is physics *only when the homogeneous problem has the zero
solution*. Logged as the general lesson: **structural priors need a
per-problem correctness check — a contract can be exactly enforced and
exactly wrong.** The candidate fix (an affine zero-point: a
problem-declared homogeneous solution with the network predicting the
deviation) went to the roadmap with its Armijo bar set at the free
control's Liouville score. *(Current tables: @tbl-stream-laplace,
@tbl-stream-liouville in @sec-stream-factorization; direction 3 of the
redirected agenda closes with this entry.)*

## Iteration 27 — far-field: strong inference, three rivals {#sec-nb-iter27}

*(2026-07-05; key `iteration_27_farfield_strong_inference`; session
artifacts `farfield_inference*.json`.)*

The far-field split (0.67–0.88 across every arm) got the full
strong-inference treatment: three rival mechanisms, each with a
discriminator pre-registered before the runs. **M1 (annulus coverage)**
came back ambiguous-partial — doubling the annulus cut far-field
0.694 $\to$ 0.179, a 74% mitigation, but the model stayed 6.2$\times$
above ID *inside* the new annulus. **M2 (member decay)** came back
excluded, and with a process note worth disclosing in full: the verdict
as first coded implemented only the magnitude half of its
pre-registered rule and read "supported"; the *directional* qualifier —
written in the docstring before any measurement — flips it, because the
prediction **super**-decays (exponent $-24$ vs the exact $-2$) while
the member basis is exactly analytic on $[4,12]$: the pathology decays
too *fast* to live in member tails. The qualifier was applied
post-measurement as pre-written, and the annulus-8 edge-tracking below
corroborates the alternative independently. **M3 (coefficient
extrapolation)** got the smoking gun: the output-projection sigmoid
gate collapses at the training edge (0.52 $\to$ 0.010 $\to$
$2.3\times10^{-17}$ from $r$ = 1.1 to 12; local exponents
$-13/-26/-51$), and on the annulus-8 checkpoint the collapse onset
**moves to the new training edge** — the pathology tracks the training
boundary, not the dictionary. Follow-up pre-registered: bound the gate;
falsifier — no improvement means the gate is symptom, not cause.

## Iteration 28 — the gate fix fires its falsifier {#sec-nb-iter28}

*(2026-07-05; key `iteration_28_bounded_gate`.)*

The fix worked. The model got worse. Compactified gate inputs
($v \to v/\sqrt{1+|v|^2}$) removed the saturation regime exactly as
designed (gate trace smooth and nonzero) — and far-field went 0.694
$\to$ **2.98**, 4.3$\times$ worse. The surprise that redirected the
ladder: **the collapse was load-bearing.** The saturating gate had been
*suppressing* polynomially growing query-side direct-drive linear
branches (a `vector_from_scalar` branch grows 0.026 at $r$ = 1.1 to
1.45 at $r$ = 12; lifted drive norms grow like $r$–$r^2$). Root cause
corrected: not the gate, not the branches, but the **pair** of
unbounded radial dependences. Silver lining kept for the config: the
bounded gate improves in-annulus accuracy (ID 0.0215 vs 0.0269,
circulation-OOD 0.018 vs 0.033). Next rung pre-registered: bound the
query-side inputs *at the source* so every learned coefficient sees
bounded invariants.

## Iteration 29 — bound at the source; the residual isolated {#sec-nb-iter29}

*(2026-07-05; key `iteration_29_source_bounded_query`.)*

The injected query position compactified
($x \to x/\sqrt{1+|x|^2}$, equivariant), with the kernel members
verified **bitwise-pinned** to raw positions — the physics path exact,
the learned path bounded. It did exactly what it claims: coefficient
traces flat to $r$ = 12 (far/near ratio 1.03) — **M3 excluded by
construction**, the first outright exclusion of the ladder's lead
suspect. Far-field: 0.452 — between the pre-registered bars, partial.
The residual is thereby *isolated* as representational (M2's territory
after all, one level up from member tails): **bounded is not decaying**
— the direct-drive part converges to a direction-dependent constant
($\approx$0.24, exponent $\approx$0) where the exact field decays
$r^{-2}$, and the single-layer $\log r$ tail (state norm 2.4 at
$r$ = 12) is fit only by near-cancellation in-annulus. Honest
decomposition logged: far-field error = coefficient extrapolation
(fixed by construction) + missing decay structure (coverage or explicit
structure).

## Iteration 30 — decay structure; the ladder closes at five seeds {#sec-nb-iter30}

*(2026-07-05; key `iteration_30_decay_structure` +
`five_seed_close`.)*

Two exact structures, both licensed for zero-net-flux exteriors only,
zero parameters added: the $r^{-2}$ **direct-drive envelope**
($1/(1+|x|^2)$ — the leading order of a 2D exterior zero-flux velocity
is the doublet; the direct drive may not outlive it) and the
**monopole-free single-layer deflation** (measure-weighted rank-one;
exact zero net charge per member, so the $\log r$ tail is dead for
*any* coefficients — with the corollary that the 2D log gauge cancels
and the deflated member is exactly similarity invariant). Seed 17:
far-field 0.133, chain 0.694 $\to$ 2.98 $\to$ 0.452 $\to$ 0.133 —
the $<$0.35 bar met, not yet the $<$0.10 fully-fixed bar; seeds 18–21
launched (p19b).

**Five-seed close: far-field 0.090 $\pm$ 0.048** — the fully-fixed bar
crossed at the mean (per-seed 0.036/0.061/0.074/0.133/0.147; two seeds
above 0.10, stated plainly), 7.7$\times$ at an *unchanged* training
annulus, beating the coverage lever (0.179), with every other split at
family-best (ID 0.0174, circulation-OOD 0.0168, geometry 0.0303). The
four physics-licensed knobs — bounded gate, bounded query source,
$r^{-2}$ envelope, monopole-free single layer — compose into a strictly
dominant configuration. Remaining leak, logged for the roadmap: the
$r^{-1}$ member tails still reach $r^{-2}$ only through fitted
zero-circulation cancellation. *(Current section, table, and figure:
@sec-farfield-ladder, @tbl-farfield-close.)*

## Iteration 31 — heads versus rank: the last loose end {#sec-nb-iter31}

*(2026-07-04; key `iteration_31_heads_vs_rank`; pre-registered design in
`studies/heads_rank_study.py`; session artifacts
`scratch/brev/results/p20_headsrank`, jobs `p20_hr_*`.)*

The one still-unrun probe of the component-eval direction. The design
review had proved heads and separable rank enter one layer's score
identically — the pair-coefficient class depends only on
$H(R_0 + DR_1)$ — so the head count *should* be capacity bookkeeping.
But heads stay distinct after the scores (head-blocked value spaces,
head-by-head typed output contractions), so a measured difference could
only live there. Three singpair arms at total score capacity exactly 80
(the ranks divide evenly): the reference $H{=}4$, $12/4$ (104,537
params); $H{=}1$, $48/16$ (104,123, $-0.40$%); $H{=}8$, $6/2$ (104,897,
$+0.34$%). Laplace reference bank, 3,000 steps, seeds 17/29/43, the
iteration-26 evaluation bank. Rule pre-registered: match = 3-seed mean
within $2\times$ the larger seed sd, per arm per split; any decisive
miss localizes the effect in the per-head value/output structure.

Provenance anchor for free: the $H{=}4$ arm reproduced iteration 26's
two-stream row to all four archived decimals (ID 0.0485, geometry
0.0686, freq-OOD 0.2111) — same seeds, same bank, unchanged arm.

**The verdict split down the middle, and the split is the finding.**
$H{=}8$ at halved ranks: within tolerance on every split (largest
$|\Delta|$ 0.0050, on stronger deformation against a 0.0296 tolerance)
— the redundancy claim holds in that direction. $H{=}1$ at quadrupled ranks: **better**, decisively
on ID (0.0413 vs 0.0485, $\Delta$ $-0.0072$ vs tolerance $\pm 0.0050$,
2.9$\times$ the reference seed sd, a 15% error reduction), directionally
better on all four splits, most seed-stable (geometry sd 0.0018 vs
0.0070; freq-OOD 0.0158 vs 0.0523), with the fewest parameters. Since
the score class is matched by construction, the gain prices exactly the
head-blocking of the value/output maps: one full-width head (48/12
value channels) beats four aligned blocks. The pre-registered
"heads are bookkeeping" verdict is therefore **refused** in the
direction nobody worried about — the restriction is the heads
themselves, mildly. Logged for the roadmap rather than acted on: one
PDE, one capacity point, three seeds; flipping the reference config
wants at least the screened/3D suites first. *(Current table:
@tbl-heads-vs-rank in @sec-heads-vs-rank; the component-eval direction
of @sec-future closes fully with this entry.)*

## Iteration 32 — one head across suites: flip on parsimony, win stays home {#sec-nb-iter32}

*(2026-07-04; key `iteration_32_one_head_cross_suite`; pre-registered
design and flip rule in `studies/one_head_cross_suite.py`; session
artifacts `scratch/brev/results/p21_onehead`, jobs `p21_oh_*`.)*

The suites iteration 31 asked for. One capacity-preserving one-head
variant per suite — heads $4 \to 1$, ranks $12/4 \to 48/16$; the
identity $4(12 + D\,4) = 1(48 + D\,16)$ holds the score-coefficient
class fixed in every spatial dimension, so the arms again differ only
in the un-blocked value/output maps — wired into three drivers
(`mesh_transformer_kernel_singonly_h1` on screened,
`mesh_transformer_kernel_singpair_pseudo_h1` on potential-flow velocity
with the pseudo sector untouched, `mesh_transformer_kernel_singpair_h1`
on 3D), three seeds each, against the **archived** h4 comparators
(iterations 13, 23, 16; protocols matched run-for-run, nothing
re-trained). Rule pre-registered for a *default change*: per split, one
head passes iff mean minus archived mean $\le 2\times$ the larger seed
sd; flip iff every split of $\ge 2$ suites passes and no split anywhere
is a decisive loss; any decisive loss $\to$ heads stay at four,
iteration 31 recorded as Laplace-specific.

**The falsifier did not fire — and neither did the win.** All 13 cells
pass (3/3 suites), so the verdict is
`flip_default_to_one_head`: the documented reference configuration now
carries one full-width head (81,961 $\to$ 81,547 parameters; the frozen
benchmark capacity configs and every archived arm stay bitwise). But
the honest half of the entry is the direction: one head is worse on 11
of 13 cells — screened ID 0.0205 vs 0.0099 ($+0.0107$ against a 0.0135
tolerance, 1.6$\times$ the larger sd, the closest call of the study),
pf-velocity ID 0.0321 vs 0.0278, 3D sphere 0.0093 vs 0.0064 — with the
only two directionally-better cells both mode-OOD (screened unseen
modes $-0.0006$, 3D star unseen modes $-0.0101$). The iteration-31 15%
ID gain is hereby recorded as **Laplace-specific**; what traveled is
non-inferiority. Also named: the tolerance keys to the *larger* sd of
the two arms, so the one-head arm's own seed spread (2.3$\times$ the
archived on screened ID) buys it slack — a rule bias to fix if this
recurs. Composition check passed en route: `drive_pseudo_dim=8` rides
the one-head trade unchanged (per-head pseudo split $2 \to 8$),
circulation-OOD staying at the typed level (0.0476 vs 0.0371, within
tolerance). Standing falsifier: any future decisive one-head loss
reverts the flip. *(Current section and table:
@sec-one-head-cross-suite, @tbl-one-head-cross-suite; reference

## Iteration 33 — rotational Euler: real vorticity, exact labels {#sec-nb-iter33}

*(2026-07-04; key `iteration_33_euler_rotational`; driver
`problems/euler_rotational.py`; session artifacts
`scratch/brev/results/p22_euler_rotational`, jobs `p22_er_*`.)*

The first genuinely **rotational** steady Euler benchmark — every fluid
suite so far was irrotational. The construction: steady 2D Euler admits
solutions with vorticity constant along streamlines,
$\omega = F(\psi)$; the linear choice $F(\psi) = c^2\psi$ turns the
streamfunction equation into Helmholtz, $\Delta\psi + c^2\psi = 0$ —
Bessel $J_m$ series on disks, the oscillatory sibling of screened's
$I_m/K_m$ machinery, with $u = (\psi_y, -\psi_x)$ carrying the exact
iteration-21/23 typing ($\psi$ pseudoscalar, $u$ polar). Pressure from
the rotational Bernoulli relation, derived and then **certified before
anything trained**: $\nabla(p + |u|^2/2) = -F(\psi)\nabla\psi$ gives
$H(\psi) = -c^2\psi^2/2$ ($H_0 = 0$ gauge), and float64 autograd put the
steady-momentum residual $\|(u\cdot\nabla)u + \nabla p\| /
\|(u\cdot\nabla)u\|$ at $2.2$–$7.9\times10^{-16}$ across all four
splits (threshold $10^{-10}$), incompressibility $\sim\!10^{-16}$,
Helmholtz $<5\times10^{-15}$ — rotational Euler with no CFD solver in
the label chain. Well-posedness stated honestly: the family poses the
learning problem $\{$boundary velocity, $\tilde c\} \to$ interior
fields on certified exact solutions, with every split strictly below
the first disk Dirichlet eigenvalue $j_{0,1} = 2.4048$ (at eigenvalues
boundary data does not determine the interior; the near-eigenvalue tier
$[2.25, 2.38]$ was kept only after its certification passed).

Pre-registered: **the wall's third instance** — boundary velocity is
the only drive, pressure is exactly drive-quadratic, phases are
negation-symmetric, so the linear arm's pressure must pin at 1.0.
Also logged in advance: no wall exists for the $0o$ arm (polar in,
polar out); `drive_pseudo_dim=8` is a representational probe — the
natural latent $\psi$ is exactly a wedge-sourced pseudoscalar. Arms on
the flipped one-head reference (first new family after iteration 32).

**Runs (3 seeds, 3,000 steps, ~6 min/run on the A100).** The wall held
**bitwise**: twelve of twelve linear pressure cells at 1.000, worst
deviation $7\times10^{-4}$. Nonlinear breaks it (pressure ID 0.181);
the $0o$ arm nearly halves it again (0.103) and is the most
Euler-consistent arm (momentum-consistency 0.23 vs 0.41 vs the linear
control's 0.98 — the wall read through the physics column). The honest
half-miss: the pre-registration said the linear arm's velocity would
*match* the nonlinear arms'; it **beat** them 2.3$\times$ (0.026 vs
0.061) and degraded gracefully on every axis (worst split 0.26).

The iteration's find is the failure mode. On the near-eigenvalue tier
the nonlinear arms did not degrade — they **detonated**: relative
errors $10^{6}$–$10^{13}$ (nonlinear) and $10^{6}$–$10^{10}$ ($0o$) on
cases the linear arm handles at 0.2, with milder echoes on the other
OOD axes (seed-29 unseen-modes 352; one $0o$ seed at 9.9/22). Because
the velocity map is genuinely drive-linear, the discriminator is clean:
same cases, same physics, representable in both modes — the blowup
prices the **zero-preserving nonlinear read-in's operator-parameter
extrapolation**, not the problem. This sharpens iteration 25's
circulation-OOD anomaly (there a training transient that resolved; here
a structural liability that best-checkpoint selection does not remove)
and hands direction 7's amplitude-extrapolation item a second, sharper
axis. *(Current section, figure, and table: @sec-euler-rotational,
@fig-euler-rotational, @tbl-euler-rotational.)*

## Iteration 34 — nonlinear fragility: one engine behind two blowups {#sec-nb-iter34}

*(2026-07-04; session artifact
`results/nonlinear_fragility_2026-07-04.json`; pre-registered design in
`studies/nonlinear_fragility.py`; retraining jobs `p23_*`, artifacts
`scratch/brev/results/p23_nonlinear_fragility` — p13/p22 archived only
JSON reports, so the two nonlinear arms were retrained bitwise-identically
with `--save-checkpoint`.)*

The diagnosis rung for the nonlinear mode's two extrapolation failures:
the Euler–Bernoulli **amplitude** axis (circulation-OOD stuck at ~0.35
for the best arm; early-training blowups of 37–147) and the
rotational-Euler **operator-parameter** axis (near-eigenvalue detonations
of $10^{6}$–$10^{13}$ at full training, @sec-nb-iter33). Three rivals,
pre-registered discriminators, decisive-outcome rules written before
measurement: **N1**, implicit drive degree (the multiplicative read-in
composes to high polynomial degree in the drive; training suppresses the
high-degree terms on-range without removing them); **N2**,
operator-conditioning extrapolation (the $\tilde c$-conditioned
coefficients diverge — the operator-stream analog of the far-field gate
pathology); **N3**, physical-amplification tracking (the model chases the
true $1/J_0(\tilde c)$ growth with an unbounded parameterization).

**Verdicts, all three decisive.** **N1 supported**: at fixed geometry,
scaling the joint drive $(U, \Gamma)$ and log-log-fitting the response
put the trained nonlinear arm's effective drive degree at **21.3
(velocity, target exactly 1)** and **20.8 (pressure, target exactly 2)**
over $\alpha \in [2, 4]$ — on-range the fits read 1.56 and 3.82, so
training had tamed the degree where the data lives and nowhere else (the
step-200 snapshot reads 18.1/17.4: the degree is there from the start;
what "resolved" by 3,000 steps was only its on-range amplitude).
**N2 excluded**: sweeping $\tilde c$ through the near-eigenvalue band at
bitwise-pinned drive moved no trace — worst near/train ratio 1.61 across
the entire conditioned stack (coefficients, gates, operator states,
outputs); the conditioning continues smoothly through the band edge.
**N3 supported**: near-eigenvalue cases renormalized by the exact
homogeneity factors ($u/A$, $p/A^2$) evaluate at **0.240** where the raw
cases read $5.6\times10^{6}$, with error $\sim A^{5.9}$ beyond the band.

The synthesis is the iteration's finding: with N2 excluded and the
renormalized error ordinary, the parameter-axis failure is **the
amplitude axis in disguise** — the physical amplification (up to
77$\times$) feeds the near-eigenvalue *drive*, and N1's implicit degree
detonates on it (recorded cross-axis probe: the rotational checkpoint's
amplitude response runs at slope ~23.6 out to $\alpha = 128$). One
engine, two symptoms: **the zero-preserving nonlinear read-in has
implicit drive degree ~21 against targets of degree 1 and 2.** A
degree-21 monomial amplifies $2\times$ drive by $2\times10^{6}$ — the
measured $10^{3}$ at $\alpha \approx 2.2$ and $10^{8}$ at $\alpha = 4$
are not pathology on top of the mechanism; they *are* the mechanism. No
fix was attempted in this iteration; the fix rung (declare the degree)
follows as iteration 35. *(Current section: @sec-nonlinear-fragility.)*

## Iteration 35 — declare the degree: the fix rung {#sec-nb-iter35}

*(2026-07-05; key `iteration_35_declared_degree`; acceptance study
`studies/declared_degree.py`, artifact
`results/declared_degree_2026-07-05.json`; jobs `p24_{eb,er}_q2_s*` and
`p24_eb_q2p_s*` on `mesh-xform-a100`.)*

If the engine is implicit degree, the principled fix mirrors how the
architecture declares linearity: **declare the degree**. New field mode
`field_mode="quadratic"` — the drive path is the *linear* machinery end
to end (drive lift, `LinearMeshFieldBlock` stack, linear kernel decode;
reusing it is what makes the contract provable) plus **exactly one**
bilinear, operator-conditioned typed composition at the query read-in,
$F = u + s \odot g(\mathrm{op}) \odot B(L_2u, L_3u)$, drawn from the
closed $\{0e, 0o, 1o\}$ product set (`QuadraticFieldReadIn`, a third
class per the one-class-per-contract discipline — not a flag on the
nonlinear block). Output: an exact degree-$\le 2$ polynomial in the
drive *for any weights*. Zero-preservation inherited; placement at the
read-in rather than in a stackable block is load-bearing (residual
bilinear updates would compose to $2^k$ — the escalation being
forbidden); a query-side composition spans products of boundary
integrals ($|u(x)|^2$), which boundary-local products cannot. Design
generalizes to declared degree $k$ (graded states, $k-1$ compositions);
$k = 2$ built, matching every current target. Knob discipline held:
linear/nonlinear paths bitwise unchanged (the p23 checkpoints reproduce
their archived reproduction numbers to the last digit under the new
code).

Pre-registered before the runs, measured after (3 seeds × 3,000 steps
per suite, arms otherwise identical to the archived nl configs):

- **Structural degree — passed at machine precision.** The iteration-34
  probe, now the acceptance test: trained q2 checkpoints in float64 fit
  $c_1\alpha + c_2\alpha^2$ with worst relative residual
  $2.1\times10^{-15}$ (bar $10^{-9}$), slopes **1.00/2.00** on- and
  off-range, every seed, both suites (nl: 21.3/20.8); exactly zero at
  zero drive. A standing unit test runs the same probe on both modes —
  the nonlinear mode fails it by eleven orders, so the instrument
  discriminates.
- **Rotational near-eigenvalue — bar passed, stretch missed, and the
  miss is informative.** $10^{6}$–$10^{13}$ $\to$ **0.670 ± 0.111**
  (bar $< 1.0$). The stretch (0.24–0.30, iteration 34's
  renormalized-ordinary level) was not reached — but the *velocity*
  reaches 0.216 while the $A^2$-amplified pressure sits at 0.686: what
  remains is conditioning accuracy under 150–6,000$\times$ target
  amplitude, not degree (the same checkpoints show no response above
  degree 2). Unseen-modes 160 ± 178 $\to$ 0.144 ± 0.013; ID *better*
  than nl (0.072 vs 0.112 combined) at 122k vs 173k parameters.
- **EB circulation-OOD — the parity lesson recurs, composed.** The
  untyped q2 lands at 0.682 ± 0.003 — exactly the iteration-23 parity
  floor (velocity 0.6485 vs 0.647): the split's residual for untyped
  arms is parity, not degree, so the pre-registered 0.35 comparator
  (the *typed* nl arm) demands the matched-typing subject. Launched
  mid-iteration and logged as such: `mt_singpair_q2_pseudo` (declared
  degree *and* declared parity). **The composed arm crosses the bar:
  circulation-OOD 0.086 ± 0.059** (per-seed 0.154/0.044/0.061; bar
  $< 0.15$ at the mean, one seed above) vs the typed nl arm's
  0.352 ± 0.110 — with ID *better* (0.032 vs 0.046 combined; pressure
  0.035 vs 0.063) and the same $10^{-15}$/1.000/2.000 structural
  contract. Meanwhile the untyped comparison is itself a result: q2
  dominates untyped nl on every split (circulation 0.682 ± 0.003 vs
  0.93 ± 0.40 — better *and* 130$\times$ more seed-stable; ID 0.161 vs
  0.177). Ops note for the record: the three q2p jobs launched
  concurrently thrashed the 28 vCPUs (~20$\times$ slowdown; the
  drivers are sample-generation-bound on CPU); killed and relaunched
  sequentially, each solo run took 4.3 minutes.
- **The falsifier did not fire.** No off-range detonation exists
  anywhere in the q2 reports — worst split anywhere is far-field 0.78,
  a known separate axis (@sec-farfield-ladder).

The ladder closes with the program's second structural-declaration
motto instance: linearity, parity, and now polynomial degree are
properties of a *problem*, offered as contracts — and the mode that
declared the degree beat the mode that learned to suppress it, on the
suppressing mode's home turf. *(Current section, figure, and table:
@sec-nonlinear-fragility, @fig-declared-degree,
@tbl-declared-degree; roadmap update: @sec-future item 7.)*

## Iteration 36 — Navier–Stokes: the first solver-labeled suite {#sec-nb-iter36}

*(2026-07-05; key `iteration_36_navier_stokes`; solver
`datasets/fem_navier_stokes.py`, generator family `ns_cavity_star` in
`datasets/generate_datasets.py`, driver `datasets/dataset_train_ns.py`;
verification artifact `results/ns_solver_verification_2026-07-05.json`;
jobs `p25_{verify,gen,train}` on `mesh-xform-a100`.)*

Every label so far was either closed-form or a *linear* solve
(iteration 17's Laplace catalog). This iteration crosses the program's
next ledge: steady incompressible Navier–Stokes — $-\nu\Delta u +
(u\cdot\nabla)u + \nabla p = 0$, $\nabla\cdot u = 0$ — solved by a
Taylor–Hood P2–P1 FEM with analytic-Jacobian Newton on the bank's
star domains, with a smooth band-limited **tangential** boundary
velocity localized on an arc (driven-lid-like; tangential-only makes
$\oint u\cdot n\,ds = 0$ exact at the continuous level, and the
mean-pressure Lagrange multiplier absorbs and *reports* the discrete
interpolation defect). $\mathrm{Re} = UL/\nu$ with peak drive speed
$U = 1$ and $L = 1$, so the operator scalar fed to every arm is the
PDE coefficient $\tilde\nu = 1/\mathrm{Re}$ (the screened-suite
convention: feed the equation's coefficient).

**Solver build log, including the dead-end.** The first assembly
produced a Newton that detonated from a garbage Stokes solve; SVD of
the reduced saddle matrix showed a *2-dimensional pressure null space
localized at two mesh corners*. Root cause (found via a local-block
Monte-Carlo cross-check): the degree-5 Dunavant rule had its two
barycentric group constants entered as $1-2a$ instead of $a$ — an
invalid rule that still passed the row-sum and $B\,x = E$ identity
checks (both are symmetry-insensitive). Lesson recorded: quadrature
constants need an exactness test over the full monomial basis
(`test_quadrature_rule_is_exact_to_degree_five` now integrates every
$l_1^i l_2^j$, $i+j \le 5$, to 1e-14). After the fix, everything
snapped to theory in one step.

**Verification (bars from the task, measured before any dataset was
generated).** MMS with hand-derived forcing (the forcing itself is
certified against finite differences — protect the instrument):
velocity order **2.84**, pressure order **1.95** on the unit square;
on a production star (1024-gon), velocity rel-L2 **4.7e-6 at the
production $h = 0.02$** and **6.2e-7 at $h = 0.01$** — the 1e-6 bar
crosses at $h \approx 0.01$, where one solve costs 359 s
(single-thread PARDISO) versus 73 s at $h = 0.02$. Decision, made on
the cost curve and logged here: **production runs at $h = 0.02$**,
where the *label-noise floor* (production vs 1.5× finer, the bar that
matters against ~1e-2 model errors) is measured per generated subset
and must land ≤ 1e-3; the 1e-6 MMS accuracy is demonstrated at
$h = 0.01$ on the same geometry rather than paid for on every one of
~1400 cases (3× generation cost for label improvements two orders
below model error). Discrete certificates per solve: momentum-balance
assembly identity ≤ 1e-11 (measured ~1e-14), gauge $\int p_h = 0$ to
roundoff, $\lambda|\Omega| = -\oint u_h\cdot n$, Newton relative
residual ≤ 1e-10. Probed Newton robustness at $h = 0.02$: Re 100 and
200 converge in 4–5 iterations with ≤ 1 backtracking step on both
train-band and 0.65-deformation stars; the full Re × deformation grid
(to 400) runs in `p25_verify`.

**The $h = 0.02$ decision was refuted by its own measurement, and
revised.** The first full catalog (1,400 cases, 19.6 minutes wall on
26 workers — the budget fear was off by 8×) came back with velocity
noise floors at $1.5$–$4.1\times10^{-4}$ as predicted, but pressure
floors at $2.6$–$3.2\times10^{-3}$ across every split: the
$8\times10^{-4}$ extrapolation from the single $h = 0.03$ probe case
(Re 156) did not survive contact with the full Re band. The
$O(h^2)$ pressure is the binding field, the target is $10^{-3}$, and
the measured generation cost made the honest fix cheap: the catalog
was **regenerated at $h = 0.0105$** (predicted pressure floor
$\approx 0.9\times10^{-3}$; measured: velocity $\le 5.8\times10^{-5}$
everywhere, pressure $\le 8.7\times10^{-4}$ on four of five splits
with the unseen-drive split's worst sampled case at
$1.26\times10^{-3}$ — the prediction held except on the roughest
drives, stated as measured), where
the MMS velocity bar of $10^{-6}$ is also met *at production
resolution* (star sweep: 6.2e-7 at $h = 0.01$, 1.36e-6 at 0.0125) —
so the production/verification two-resolution compromise recorded
above dissolved. First-pass manifest preserved at
`scratch/ns_probe/manifest_h020.json`; the memory headroom check
(PARDISO factors ~4× larger) dropped the worker count 26 → 20.

**Pre-registered before the first ns_cavity_star training run** (arms:
`mt_singpair_q2_pseudo`, `mt_singpair_nl_pseudo`, `mt_singpair_linear`,
`boundary_mean`, `transolver_intree_matched`; 15 epochs, 3 seeds
17/29/43, fixed-dataset regime of iteration 17):

- **P1, the Re-dependent linear wall.** For N-S both fields are
  nonlinear in the drive once convection matters, and the map tends to
  the exactly linear Stokes map as $\mathrm{Re} \to 0$ — so unlike the
  parity and superposition walls (all-or-nothing), this wall should
  have a *measurable height profile*: the linear arm's per-case error
  for **both velocity and pressure** grows with case Reynolds number
  and approaches the nonlinear arms' error at the low-Re end.
  Deciding measurement: per-case rel-L2 vs Re from the reports'
  `per_case` blocks (eval_id + eval_unseen_Re), binned by Re; verdict
  rule: the linear-minus-nonlinear gap at the top Re bin exceeds the
  bottom-bin gap by ≥ 3× for at least one field, and the bottom-bin
  velocity gap is small (< 2× seed sd). Falsifier: a flat or
  decreasing gap profile.
- **P2, declared degree 2 as an approximation hypothesis.** For the
  exact Euler families the pressure was *exactly* drive-quadratic —
  q2 was a contract. For N-S the solution map is analytic in the
  drive with all orders present (Stokes term linear; each convection
  correction raises the degree), so q2 is now an approximation whose
  adequacy is the experiment. Read-out rule (registered): q2_pseudo
  within 2× seed sd of nl_pseudo on eval_id combined ⇒ "degree-2
  truncation suffices at these Re"; q2 between linear and nl with a
  Re-growing gap to nl ⇒ higher orders matter and the contract's home
  turf ends at nonlinear-PDE suites.
- **P3, floors.** `boundary_mean` pressure rel-L2 exactly 1.0 (no
  pressure drive); its velocity floor is the O(2)-mean of a localized
  tangential drive — expected near 1 (the interior recirculation is
  not a constant field).
- No ordering is pre-registered for the Transolver baseline (first
  mainstream measurement on a solver-labeled nonlinear suite).

**Dataset generation (final catalog `ns_cavity_star/v1`, $h = 0.0105$).**
**1,400 converged cases** (840 train; 140 per eval split across eval_id,
eval_unseen_Re, eval_unseen_geometry, eval_unseen_drive_profile) in
**161.5 minutes wall** on 20 workers — ~138 core-seconds per case
including the coarse self-check (the instrumented solo case read 161 s).
**4 candidate attempts rejected and redrawn** across the whole catalog
(2 in unseen-Re, 1 train, 1 unseen-drive; all Newton), worst Newton
count 8, zero continuation-ladder failures, momentum-balance identity
$\le 1.4\times10^{-13}$ everywhere. Label-noise floors against the
1.5× finer companion solves: velocity **$\le 5.8\times10^{-5}$**
(every split), pressure **$\le 8.7\times10^{-4}$** on four of five
splits with the unseen-drive split's worst sampled case at
**$1.26\times10^{-3}$** — against the pre-committed $\le 10^{-3}$
bar, the bar that matters under ~$10^{-1}$ model errors. Ops note: the
generator now writes cases incrementally (imap_unordered +
write-on-arrival) after this run's invisible-progress lesson; the
change is write-plumbing only, round-trip-tested, and landed after v1
was produced.

**Pre-registered versus measured** (rules as written above, untouched;
eval_id combined rel-L2, mean ± sd over seeds 17/29/43):

- **P1, the Re-dependent linear wall — supported on pressure,
  refuted on the velocity leg.** Binning per-case errors by case
  Reynolds number puts the linear-minus-nonlinear gap ratio (top Re
  bin over bottom) at **4.19 (pressure)** against the registered
  $\ge 3\times$ bar — the wall has the predicted height profile,
  0.112 $\to$ 0.471 across Re 10 $\to$ 300. The **velocity** ratio
  reads **1.08**: flat at $\approx 0.19$ everywhere, so the bottom-bin
  smallness condition failed — Re 10 at unit drive speed is evidently
  not Stokes, and/or part of the velocity gap is a linear-read-in
  representation deficit rather than the nonlinearity wall. The
  falsifier (flat or decreasing profile) fired for one field and not
  the other; the discriminating follow-up is a genuinely Stokes band
  (Re $\le 1$), logged in @sec-future.
- **P2, declared degree 2 as an approximation — the truncation
  suffices at these Re.** eval_id combined: q2_pseudo
  **0.278 ± 0.060**, nl_pseudo **0.231 ± 0.005**, difference 0.047
  within the registered 2× seed sd. Honest texture: q2's seed spread
  is 12× the nl arm's here (seed 29 at 0.347) — the *reverse* of the
  exact-Euler suites where the declared degree was the more stable
  arm. On a map with all drive orders present, the contract buys no
  stability premium; it merely keeps pace.
- **P3, floors — exact.** `boundary_mean` pressure rel-L2 **1.000000**
  on every seed and split (combined 1.193 ± 0.000 on eval_id); the
  drive plumbing leaks nothing.

The Transolver baseline lands at **0.953 ± 0.080** eval_id combined —
above every transformer arm (0.231–0.437) and barely under the 1.19
floor; first mainstream measurement on a solver-labeled nonlinear
suite at the shared protocol, with the stated caveat that 15 epochs
may undertrain it. Per-field texture worth keeping: near-wall
velocity errors run *lower* than interior for every learning arm
(nl: 0.170 vs 0.242) — the near-wall field is drive-dominated; the
interior recirculation is the hard part.

The ledge is crossed. Every label the program trained on before this
iteration was either closed-form or one linear solve away from
closed-form; this suite's labels come out of a Newton iteration on a
nonlinear operator, certified per solve, with a measured noise floor
standing between the solver and every claim built on it. And the
contracts changed character on the way up: linearity and degree were
offered as provable properties of exact families — on Navier–Stokes
the same declarations return as *hypotheses* with measurable adequacy
and Re-dependent profiles, which is exactly the form in which they can
earn their way onto real physics. *(Current section: @sec-ns-cavity,
@fig-ns-wall, @tbl-ns-arms, @tbl-ns-ledger.)*

## Iteration 37 — the Re $\le$ 1 band and the N-S fidelity block {#sec-nb-iter37}

*(2026-07-05; key `iteration_37_lowre_band`; slice generator override in
`datasets/generate_datasets.py` (`--reynolds-range`), fidelity block in
`datasets/dataset_train_ns.py`; jobs `p26b_{gen,train}` on
`mesh-xform-a100`.)*

Two small closers for iteration 36's logged gaps — no new architecture,
no new family, just the two measurements that iteration honestly
declared missing.

**Why the velocity leg needed its own band.** P1 predicted the linear
arm's wall grows with Re *for both fields*; the pressure leg passed
(4.19$\times$) and the velocity leg was refuted — flat $\approx 0.19$
across Re 10–300. The recorded readings: (a) Re 10 at unit drive is
already convection-dominated, so the sampled band simply never
contained the Stokes regime the prediction was about; or (b) part of
the velocity gap is a linear-read-in representation deficit, not the
nonlinearity wall. The discriminator, logged then: a band where the
velocity map IS near-Stokes-linear.

**The slice.** `ns_cavity_star/v1-lowre` — 180 cases, train/eval_id at
Re log-uniform $[0.5, 5]$, eval_unseen_Re at $(5, 10]$ (directly above
the training band, abutting the production catalog's low edge at 10),
eval_unseen_geometry/drive as in the family. Same geometry and drive
distributions, same $h = 0.0105$, same per-case verification and
finer-mesh noise-floor discipline (stride 15 so every split gets
sampled). Generator change: `NSGeneratorSettings` gains
`reynolds_range`/`unseen_reynolds_range` overrides (the Reynolds band
is the *only* movable axis — a slice differs from production in
exactly one declared dimension), unit-tested for split-awareness.

**Pre-registered before the first v1-lowre training run** (rule also in
`scratch/brev/p26b_aggregate.py`'s docstring, written before launch):
if the velocity map is near-Stokes-linear at Re $\le 1$, the linear
arm's velocity error approaches the nl arm's (gap $\to \sim 0$) at the
low end and grows monotonically along Re. Deciding numbers on the
joined per-case gap curve (gap $=$ linear $-$ nl_pseudo per log-Re
bin, seeds pooled, eval_id + eval_unseen_Re; v1 side from the archived
iteration-36 reports):

- **P1v-a (Stokes approach):** bottom joined bin (Re $\in [0.5, \sim
  1)$) velocity gap $\le 0.05$ absolute AND $\le 0.25\times$ the
  top-bin gap.
- **P1v-b (graded growth):** gap monotonically nondecreasing along the
  joined bins (0.02 noise tolerance) and top-bin $\ge 3\times$
  bottom-bin (iteration 36's registered ratio bar, now on the
  completed band).
- **Falsifier** (reading (b), the representation deficit): bottom-bin
  velocity gap $\ge 0.1$.

The nonlinear reference is nl_pseudo alone; on the archived v1 bins
the min over {nl, q2} that iteration 36 used equals nl everywhere, so
the conventions coincide. Arms: `mt_singpair_linear`,
`mt_singpair_nl_pseudo`, 15 epochs, seeds 17/29/43 — the exact
iteration-36 protocol on the slice.

**The fidelity block (deliverable 2), built and certified before the
runs.** `dataset_train_ns.py` now emits the @sec-fidelity-columns
block on solver-labeled data: the strong-form momentum residual of the
model's OWN prediction, $\tilde\nu\Delta u - (u\cdot\nabla)u -
\nabla p$ by float64 autograd at a deterministic 32-query interior
subsample of two cases per split, normalized by the prediction's own
advection norm $\|(u\cdot\nabla)u\|$ (the euler-driver convention; a
closed-form scale does not exist on a solver-labeled family), plus
$L\,\|\nabla\cdot u\|/\|u\|$. The coefficient $\tilde\nu = 1/\mathrm{Re}$
is read from the CASE — the model never sees the governing equations,
the metric does. Instrument certification, in-tree
(`test_fidelity_residuals_certify_the_instrument`): the exact
Kovasznay solution — whose $\lambda$ depends on $\nu$ — scores
$< 10^{-8}$ *only* if the metric uses the case viscosity, and a rigid
rotation with dropped pressure scores exactly 1.0 (the residual *is*
the advection term). One honest limitation recorded in the driver
docstring: a constant velocity with zero pressure zeroes the interior
strong form (it fails the boundary conditions, not the PDE), so the
block complements, never replaces, the $L^2$ columns. The
iteration-36 archived runs predate the block — em-dash in their table
column, per the @sec-fidelity-columns convention.

**Generation.** 180/180 converged in **898 s wall** on 20 workers
(~100 core-seconds per case — the near-Stokes Newton converges from
the Stokes guess in $\le 2$ iterations everywhere, 0 rejections, 0
continuation solves). Label-noise floors against the 1.5$\times$ finer
companions: velocity $\le 6.1\times10^{-5}$, pressure
$\le 5.0\times10^{-4}$ — both under the family's $10^{-3}$ bar on
every split, so the low-Re labels are *better* than the production
catalog's (the pressure floor improves with $\nu$).

**Pre-registered versus measured — the falsifier fired.** Joined
velocity gap (linear $-$ nl_pseudo, per log-Re bin, Re 0.5 $\to$ 300):

| Re bin center | 0.79 | 1.6 | 3.3 | 6.7 | 14 | 28 | 55 | 108 | 213 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| velocity gap | 0.184 | 0.150 | 0.127 | 0.125 | 0.189 | 0.219 | 0.211 | 0.225 | 0.204 |
| pressure gap | $-0.006$ | 0.020 | $-0.042$ | 0.148 | 0.112 | 0.233 | 0.368 | 0.545 | 0.471 |

: The completed P1 measurement (v1-lowre bins 1–4, archived-v1 bins
5–9; per-case means, seeds pooled). {#tbl-nb-iter37-gaps}

- **P1v-a (Stokes approach): FAILED.** Bottom-bin velocity gap 0.184
  against the 0.05 bar; ratio top/bottom 1.10 against 3$\times$. The
  registered falsifier (bottom gap $\ge 0.1$) fired: even where the
  velocity map is genuinely near-Stokes-linear, the linear arm trails
  by the same $\approx 0.18$ as at Re 300. **Reading (b) of the
  iteration-36 anomaly survives strong inference:** the flat velocity
  gap is a linear-read-in representation/optimization deficit on this
  family (entangled with the pseudo sector and the 233k-vs-106k
  parameter difference between the arms), not the nonlinearity wall.
- **The pressure leg completes cleanly.** Gap zero within seed noise
  across Re $< 5$ (the linear arm *wins* two of three bins: $-0.006$,
  $+0.020$, $-0.042$) rising to 0.47–0.54 at the top — the graded,
  physics-tracking wall, measured end to end. The zero-gap pressure
  bins double as the control that kills reading (a) for velocity: the
  protocol and capacity budget demonstrably let the linear arm match
  the nonlinear arm on this band when the map is near-linear.
- **Fidelity block, first population** (eval_id, mean over seeds):
  momentum residual nl **16.1** vs linear **47.7**; divergence norm
  nl **1.07** vs linear **2.70**. Large by construction near Stokes —
  the advection normalizer amplifies second-derivative error by
  $\tilde\nu/\|(u\cdot\nabla)u\|$ — and the message matches every
  fidelity measurement since the column became first-class: the
  $L^2$-fit fields do not satisfy the operator, and the nonlinear
  arm's 3$\times$ advantage tracks its velocity lead.

Absolute levels on the slice (eval_id combined: linear 0.479 ± 0.014,
nl 0.481 ± 0.037 — the nl arm's *combined* tie is a pressure trade;
its velocity is 0.297 vs 0.453) run well above the production
catalog's, as expected from a 108-case train split; only gaps cross
the catalog seam. P1 is now closed as a *split* verdict: **supported
on pressure (graded wall, 0 $\to$ 0.5 across Re 0.5–300), refuted on
velocity (flat gap, arm deficit — an architecture question, not a
physics one)**. The open question it leaves is a component-eval one:
what about the linear velocity read-in loses 0.18 on a solver-labeled
family it can representably fit at low Re — the read-in itself, or
the missing pseudo sector and parameters the nl arm carries?
Discriminating those needs a linear arm *with* the pseudo channels
(drive-linear but capacity-matched), logged as the natural follow-up,
not run here — run as iteration 38 (@sec-nb-iter38), which revised
this entry's velocity reading. *(Current section:
@sec-ns-lowre, @fig-ns-lowre-gap, @tbl-ns-lowre.)*

## Iteration 38 — the linear+pseudo confound check: the revision fired {#sec-nb-iter38}

*(2026-07-05; key `iteration_38_linear_pseudo_confound`; new arm in

One small closer, run exactly as iteration 37 logged it. Iteration
37's velocity verdict — the flat Stokes-band gap is a linear-read-in
representation deficit — rested on an arm pair that differed in
**three** things: read-in class (linear vs zero-preserving nonlinear),
parity machinery (no pseudo sector vs `drive_pseudo_dim=8`), and
capacity (106,408 vs 233,108 params). The fair control isolates the
read-in class: `mt_singpair_linear_pseudo`, the identical linear
field mode (exact drive superposition; the new in-tree structural
test certifies it stays odd-in-the-drive with the pseudo sector
attached) plus `drive_pseudo_dim=8`. Parameters: **131,248** — the
pseudo sector adds 24,840 to the linear arm, and the remaining
101,860 to nl_pseudo *is* the nonlinear read-in stack, i.e. the
treatment variable. As matched as the mode allows; a width-matched
233k linear control was not run (caveat in the archive entry).

**Pre-registered before the first linear_pseudo run** (rule in the
driver's `linear_pseudo_confound_check` design note and
`scratch/brev/p27_aggregate.py`, both outcomes stated in advance), on
the joined gap curve (linear_pseudo $-$ nl_pseudo per log-Re bin,
seeds pooled, eval_id + eval_unseen_Re, iteration-37 binning):

- **REVISION**: bottom joined-bin velocity gap $\le 0.05$ (against
  iteration 37's measured 0.184) — the deficit was parity/capacity;
  iteration 37's velocity reading is revised (the linear read-in
  class is fine where the physics is linear).
- **STANDS** (falsifier of the revision): bottom-bin gap $\ge 0.1$ —
  the read-in-class reading survives, now unconfounded.

Protocol: the new arm trained on BOTH catalogs (v1-lowre, 108-case
train split; v1, 840-case), 15 epochs, seeds 17/29/43 — the exact
iteration-36/37 protocol; comparator curves re-aggregated from the
archived reports at identical binning (the plain linear arm's
bottom-bin gap reproduces at 0.1845 — the instrument is stable).

**Measured — the revision fired.** Joined velocity gap
